key_insight: Swarmlet couples GPU-resident vortex-particle aerodynamics with flight dynamics and control to simulate multirotor wakes from individual propellers to 100-vehicle formations.
engineering_relevance: The solver supports analysis of rotor performance, wake interactions and closed-loop multirotor formations on a single GPU.
method: Meshless reformulated vortex particle LES with compact-support cores and a treecode far field free of regularization error.
Dynamic eddy viscosity, core spreading and strength relaxation with corrections conserving total vorticity and linear impulse.
Three rotor-model fidelities coupled to six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control, with connected circulation shedding.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show agreement with direct summation to 5×10⁻⁷, third-order time convergence, hover thrust within 2% without calibration, calibrated thrust and torque within 3.2%, and near-wake relative L² differences of 0.08–0.21 against particle image velocimetry.
watch_item: The 100-quadrotor demonstration uses a coarser setting; the abstract does not establish swarm-scale accuracy comparable to the propeller and near-wake validation.
paper_title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
